judgment.rationale: Both are Class-5 Content statements (rank 4) under Competency C-4.4 'Develops strategies to estimate time' within CG-4 measurement. The second SFI ('Time duration in hours and minutes', LC 'Estimate time duration in hours and minutes') establishes the underlying quantity concept of elapsed time expressed in mixed hour/minute units; the first SFI ('Solve problems involving time in daily life contexts using multiplication and division', LCs decomposing into multiplicative and divisional time word problems) applies that duration understanding within contextual multi-operation problem solving. This is a substantive extension rather than generic repetition: handling durations in hours and minutes is the quantity foundation on which multiplicative/divisional time problems in daily-life contexts operate, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first. Same-rank direction is justified by this content-specific escalation from representing duration to operating on it in applied problems, not by shared parent, page proximity, or the weak 'time'/'in' token overlaps.
